nodes.name: Pt/C RDE electrode preparation
nodes.procedure: Before drop-casting, the glassy carbon electrode (0.2463 cm²) embedded in PTFE was polished mechanically with 0.5 mm, 0.3 mm, 0.05 mm alumina powder and then sonicated in ultrapure water and isopropanol at least three times. Each time took 5 min. Ink was freshly prepared each time with 2.4 mg 47.7% Pt/C, 2.55 ml ultrapure water, 0.51 ml isopropanol and 7.65 μl 5% Nafion. The ink was sonicated in the ice-water bath for 1 h before drop-casting. Each time 5.3 μl ink was used to drop-cast on the glassy carbon electrode with a rotation rate of 450 r.p.m. to achieve a Pt loading of 8 μg cm^{-2}. The electrode was dried in the air for about 30 min before use and rinsed with ultrapure water before electrochemical conditions.

nodes.name: AEMEL Pt/C cathode preparation
nodes.procedure: The Pt/C catalyst (47.7%, TKK) and PAP-TP-85 solution were sonicated with ultrapure water and isopropanol in an ice-water bath for 2 h to obtain a well-dispersed catalyst ink. The catalyst ink was then hand-sprayed on the carbon cloth using the spray gun (iwata, HP-CS) to achieve a Pt loading of 0.12 mg cm^{-2} and ionomer loading of 25% versus catalyst. A low loading of Pt was used in the cathode here to render the HER kinetics as the limiting factor of the AEMEL performance.

nodes.source_text: The iR-corrected HOR/HER low-overpotential kinetic current density of Pt/C (8 μg_Pt cm^{-2}) with or without 10^{-5} M caffeine, 1,3-dimethyluracil, imidazole and N-methylimidazoles in H2-saturated 0.1 M KOH with a rotation rate of 2,500 r.p.m. and a scan rate of 20 mV s^{-1}, room temperature. The average i0 of Pt/C in these cases is 0.64 ± 0.02 mA cm_Pt^{-2}.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV of Pt/C in 0.1 M KOH (0.05-0.45 V vs RHE) used to derive electrochemical surface area from Hupd charge; Hupd charge suppressed by N-methylimidazoles via steric effect but HOR limiting current unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical surface area was derived from the hydrogen underpotential deposition (Hupd) charge of the cyclic voltammetry (CV) of Pt/C in 0.1 M KOH within the potential range of 0.05–0.45 V ... Although the Hupd charge of Pt/C was substantially suppressed by the N-methylimidazoles (Supplementary Fig. 2), probably via the steric effect, the HOR limiting current density remained unchanged for all cases.

nodes.characterization_summary: XAS spectrum at Pt L3-edge of Pt/C remains unchanged upon adding 10^-5 M Me-N1C2 despite suppressed Hupd peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XAS spectrum at the Pt L3-edge remains unchanged upon adding 10^-5 M Me-N1C2 onto the Pt XAS electrode despite the suppressed Hupd peaks (Supplementary Fig. 8), which suggests that the bonding between Me-N1C2 and Pt is not sufficiently strong or abundant to be detectable by the XAS

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-SEIRAS of interfacial water on Pt film in 0.1 M KOH shows ν(OH) bands at ~3500 cm^-1 (weak H-bonding water) and ~3000 cm^-1 (strongly H-bonded water near Pt); addition of 10^-5 M Me-N1C2 prevents potential-dependent decrease/blue-shift of 3000 cm^-1 band; C-H bending of CH3 at 1440 cm^-1 shows no Stark shift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic features of interfacial water, two ν(OH) bands at ~3,500 and ~3,000 cm^-1 ... However, the general trends of the ν(OH) bands are dramatically altered upon addition of 10^-5 M Me-N1C2 into 0.1 M KOH. The 3,000 cm^-1 band undergoes neither a decrease in intensity nor a blue shift with potential ... The lack of a shift of this peak [1440 cm^-1] with changing potential indicates the lack of stark effects.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ surface-enhanced Raman on Ag electrode shows ν(CH3) bands of Me-N1 between 2850-2950 cm^-1 with potential-dependent growth and broadening, while Me-N1C2 bands are preserved.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The in situ Raman spectra of Me-N1 exhibit two sets of dynamic peaks within 2,800–3,200 cm^-1 ... By contrast, the ν(CH3) bands of Me-N1C2 are largely preserved within the potential range of −0.4 to −0.1 V (Fig. 3f).
